newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses weak, markets eye Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses weak, markets eye Wall Street.

text.p: European shares slid in morning business on Friday, jolted by a near 100-point drop on Wall Street overnight, and faced a tense wait until U.S. trading resumed.
"Panic hasn't set in yet but the market is jittery," one senior London share dealer said. "Another bad day on Wall Street and we could start testing some very important chart levels."
U.S. share prices in London were lower across the board and dealers tipped Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market, to slip further but not too far.

"The futures are indicating a 40-point drop at the open," one dealer said. "We haven't seen any panic selling in Europe, just a general mark down. Hopefully that pattern will be repeated in New York today."

On a nervous currency market, the dollar traded in narrow ranges as traders focused on the European Union summit in Dublin, awaiting details of a budgetary stability pact to underpin plans for a single euro currency.
EU finance ministers held a marathon session on Thursday but left final agreement to the heads-of-government summit.

"The final pact will look far more engineered by French policymakers than German policymakers and we could see a softer mark across the board as a result," said Michael Burke, economist at Citibank in London.
French finance minister Jean Arthuis expected agreement at the summit. "There is nothing left which is of a nature to prevent an agreement (today) on the stability pact," he said.
"We have still to decide on precise figures but we are no longer far apart," German finance minister Theo Waigel added.
Investors, fearing that the New York stock market might be suffering something more serious than a passing cold, took more profits after a successful year.

Key European bourses lost more than one percent during the morning, while Asian markets also weakened but ended above their lows. However, London dealers said many institutional investors were still reluctant to sell heavily.

"Institutions aren't ready to aggressively sell," the head of trading at a major investment bank said. "People are still hoping the FTSE won't fall as much as the Dow since it (FTSE) has underperformed other markets this year."
On Thursday the Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip stocks ended down 98.81 points, or 1.54 percent, at 6,303.71 after giving back an early gain of 35 points.

It has fallen 170 points or 2.5 percent in the past two sessions, raising fears that a major correction could be due after gains of almost a third this year. London's FTSE 100 index has risen around nine percent during 1996.
A week ago markets plunged worldwide after remarks by U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan on the "irrational exuberance" of the U.S. stock market.
"Even if the Dow falls another 300 points, we're still looking at an annual gain of 20 percent, which is a good performance by anyone's standards," one London dealer said.

German shares also tracked Wall Street lower and some Frankfurt dealers feared worse to come. "After all, it's Friday the 13th," said one dealer. "I am sure there are more people out there who will come in later and sell."

In the latest news in a long-running corporate saga, German prosecutors filed criminal charges against four former General Motors executives who allegedly stole secret documents when they quit the U.S. carmaker to join rival Volkswagen. VW shares were slightly higher.
The Paris bourse was around 1.3 percent lower in active trading but brokers said signs that EU leaders were near a compromise on the stability pact lifted shares from their lows.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 112.95 yen and 1.5415 marks against 113.33 and 1.5427 in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of top British shares fell 50.6 points to 3,940.1. The 30-share DAX in Frankfurt shed 39.00 to 2,808.08.
In Paris, the CAC-40 index was 30.13 lower at 2,181.98.
Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average fell more than 500 points before reviving to end down 159.81, 0.78 percent, at 20,341.39.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold rose to $369.25/ounce from Thursday's close of $368.45. It was fixed at $369.05. Silver edged up to $4.84 from $4.82.
